messages.content: Find out about traffic laws in Texas.

function.name: lawsuit_search
function.description: Search for lawsuits related to a particular subject matter in a certain location. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

location.description: The location to perform the search in.

subject.description: The subject matter of the lawsuits.

year.description: Optional. The year in which the lawsuit was filed. Default: 2024

message.content:
Here’s a quick overview of key Texas traffic laws and regulations. For detailed statutes or legal advice, consult the Texas Transportation Code or a qualified attorney. | Topic | Key Points | Typical Penalties | |-------|------------|-------------------| | **Speed Limits** | • Posted limits apply unless otherwise specified.
• 55 mph on rural interstate highways; 45 mph on urban interstate highways.
• 35 mph on rural non‑interstate highways; 25 mph on urban non‑interstate highways.
• 25 mph on residential streets (unless posted otherwise). | • 1‑point ticket for 5–10 mph over limit.
• 2‑point ticket for 11–20 mph over.
• 3‑point ticket for >20 mph over. | | **Seat‑belt Use** | • All occupants must wear seat belts.
• Children under 4 must be in a rear‑facing child safety seat.
• Children 4–8 must be in a forward‑facing seat with a harness.
• Children 9–12 must be in a booster seat. | • $50 fine + 1 point. | | **Cell‑phone Use** | • Hand‑held use while driving is prohibited.
• Hands‑free devices allowed. | • $50 fine + 1 point. | | **Driving Under Influence (DUI)** | • Blood alcohol concentration (BAC) ≥ 0.08 % for adults.
• Lower BAC limits for commercial drivers and drivers under 21. | • First offense: $500 fine, 30‑day license suspension, possible jail.
• Subsequent offenses: higher fines, longer suspensions, mandatory alcohol‑abuse treatment. | | **Reckless Driving** | • Operating a vehicle with a willful disregard for safety. | • $500 fine, 30‑day suspension, possible jail. | | **Traffic Signal Violations** | • Running red lights, stop signs, or failing to yield. | • $200 fine, 1‑point ticket. | | **School‑Zone Speed Limits** | • 25 mph during school hours (or as posted). | • $200 fine, 1‑point ticket. | | **Parking Regulations** | • No parking in fire lanes, handicap spaces, or on sidewalks.
• Parking restrictions vary by municipality. | • $100 fine, possible towing. | | **Vehicle Registration & Inspection** | • Annual registration renewal required.
• Vehicle inspections required for certain vehicles (e.g., commercial). | • Failure to register: $100 fine + 1 point. | | **Insurance Requirements** | • Minimum liability coverage: $30,000 for bodily injury per person, $60,000 for bodily injury per accident, $25,000 for property damage. | • Failure to maintain insurance: $500 fine, license suspension. | | **Right‑of‑Way Rules** | • Yield to pedestrians at crosswalks.
• Yield to emergency vehicles with lights/alarms. | • $200 fine, 1‑point ticket. | | **Commercial Driver Regulations** | • Commercial driver’s license (CDL) required for certain vehicles.
• Hours‑of‑service rules apply. | • Violations can lead to license suspension, fines, and potential jail. | ### How to Find Specific Statutes - **Texas Transportation Code**: Available online at the Texas Legislature’s website. Search by chapter (e.g., Chapter 7 for traffic laws). - **Texas Department of Motor Vehicles (TxDMV)**: Provides guides and FAQs on licensing, registration, and insurance. - **Local Municipal Ordinances**: City or county websites often list local parking and speed‑limit ordinances. ### Quick Resources - **TxDMV Traffic Law Summary**: https://www.txdmv.gov/traffic-laws - **Texas Legislature Online**: https://statutes.capitol.texas.gov/ - **Texas DOT Traffic Safety**: https://www.txdot.gov/traffic-safety.html Feel free to ask if you need details on a specific law or how it applies to a particular situation!
